cim: University of St. Thomas Launches Master of Arts in Collaborative Intelligence
cim_eredeti: University of St. Thomas Launches Master of Arts in Collaborative Intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
The University of St. Thomas has launched a fully online Master of Arts in Collaborative Intelligence (MACI) program designed to develop artificial intelligence (AI) skills, alongside critical thinking, communication and collaboration abilities needed in today’s workplace. Designed for recent college graduates and working professionals, the degree can be completed in as little as seven months. The inaugural cohort begins spring 2027.

“AI is changing the way we work, but technology alone isn't enough,” said Dr. Candace Chou, MACI program co-director. “Employers need people who can think critically, communicate effectively and make informed decisions about how to use these tools. This program brings AI expertise together with human-centered skills to prepare graduates for today’s ever-changing workplace.”

The curriculum draws on faculty expertise from a wide variety of disciplines including education, philosophy, communication, sociology and academic technology. Students will study AI applications, ethics, workplace communication and collaborative problem-solving, applying what they learn through projects that contribute to a professional portfolio.

Designed for students from any academic or professional background, the program does not require previous AI experience or coding knowledge. Courses are offered asynchronously in seven-week blocks, allowing students to balance their studies with professional and personal commitments.

The inaugural term starts in February 2027. Undergraduate students graduating in December who apply by Jan. 17, 2027, could complete their studies by the end of the summer.
